concepts.name: NDA effective date
justifications: The agreement expressly states that its Effective Date is 1 February 2027. The parties signed earlier, on 29 January 2027, with effectiveness deferred to that date.

concepts.name: NDA permitted purpose
predicted: evaluating a possible minority investment by talus ventures ab in fjordsignal as's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
gold: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
values: Evaluating a possible minority investment by Talus Ventures AB in FjordSignal AS's marine sensor business under Project Glassfinch.
justifications: The agreement defines this as its sole Permitted Purpose.

concepts.name: NDA disclosure window end
justifications: The executed termination notice delivered on 24 November specifies an effective closing date of 30 November 2027, which is earlier than the ordinary end date.

concepts.name: NDA contractual forum
justifications: The agreement designates the courts of Oslo as the parties’ contractual forum.

concepts.name: NDA signatory entities
justifications: FjordSignal AS is identified as registered in Norway and as the Discloser.
Talus Ventures AB is identified as registered in Sweden and as the Recipient.

concepts.name: Protected assets at the April snapshot
justifications: LUMEN and SHORE remain protected as complete assets because only public or previously known components are excluded; their non-public combinations or additions are not excluded. CEDAR was still protected at the April 7 snapshot because its full public release occurred later, and BASALT’s release resulted from a breach; ORACLE’s late confirmation had not yet been accepted and MICA was independently developed without access.

concepts.name: ORACLE timely confirmation deadline
justifications: The five Business Days after the 25 March 2027 disclosure are 30 March, 31 March, 1 April, 2 April, and 5 April, excluding the specified non-Business Days. Confirmation could therefore be delivered in time through 5 April 2027.

concepts.name: ORACLE protection timeline
predicted: protection is not continuous through acceptance. oracle was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 march 2027 at 14:00 until the five-business-day confirmation deadline, 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. the confirmation was sent on 5 april at 16:58 but delivered to the designated mailbox only on 6 april at 09:05, so it was late; sending did not meet the deadline. provisional protection therefore ended at the deadline, leaving a gap until the recipient's written acceptance on 8 april at 10:00, when protection resumed prospectively. the late confirmation's delivery alone was not acceptance.
gold: oracle is provisionally protected from the 25 march oral disclosure until 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. confirmation sent before that deadline arrived late on 6 april at 09:05, so protection lapses after the deadline. it resumes prospectively when the recipient expressly accepts on 8 april at 10:00 utc; the gap is not cured retroactively.
values: Protection is not continuous through acceptance. ORACLE was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 March 2027 at 14:00 until the five-Business-Day confirmation deadline, 5 April 2027 at 17:00 UTC. The confirmation was sent on 5 April at 16:58 but delivered to the designated mailbox only on 6 April at 09:05, so it was late; sending did not meet the deadline. Provisional protection therefore ended at the deadline, leaving a gap until the Recipient's written acceptance on 8 April at 10:00, when protection resumed prospectively. The late confirmation's delivery alone was not acceptance.
justifications: The agreement makes timely delivery of written confirmation necessary for continuous protection from the oral disclosure, and says late confirmation ends provisional protection at the deadline. It expressly treats written acceptance—not sending or mere receipt—as restoring protection prospectively, without covering the gap.

concepts.name: Entire SHORE package excluded by prior possession
justifications: Prior possession is established only for the smaller S-17 module incorporated into SHORE. The package also contains new non-public information and a combination not shown to have been previously possessed, so the prior-possession exclusion does not cover the complete package.

concepts.name: CEDAR end of protection
justifications: The entire schedule was independently and lawfully released to the unrestricted public on this date, establishing the public-information exclusion for all of CEDAR. Protection therefore ended then, notwithstanding the ordinary duration period.

concepts.name: People permitted LUMEN access at the September snapshot
justifications: Elin meets the employee, undertaking, security-check, and named clean-room approval requirements. Marek qualifies as an affiliate employee because the Recipient controls 52% of Talus Research AB's votes at the snapshot, and all his access requirements are effective; Oskar qualifies as a professional adviser with an enforceable duty of confidence and the required security check and named approval.

concepts.name: Talus Research qualifying voting percentage
justifications: At the access snapshot, 48% of the votes are held directly and a presently effective, irrevocable proxy covers a disjoint additional 4%. Both count under the voting-power test, totaling 52%.

concepts.name: Marek earliest authorised LUMEN access
justifications: Talus Research qualifies as an Affiliate because the Recipient can exercise 52% of its votes while the irrevocable proxy is effective. Marek’s undertaking and security check were effective earlier, but his named clean-room approval did not take effect until 14 September, when all required conditions were met.

concepts.name: Executed competitor consent date for Pia
Q-27 notice deadline date
justifications: Because notice was initially prohibited, the deadline is the earlier of six continuous hours after the prohibition was lifted and the required production time. Six hours after the prohibition was lifted at 11:20 on 5 July is 17:20 that day, earlier than production on 6 July.

concepts.name: Q-27 notice lateness in minutes
justifications: The notice deadline was the earlier of six continuous hours after the prohibition was lifted (17:20 on 5 July) and the production time. The notice actually arrived at 17:55, 35 minutes after the deadline.

concepts.name: Q-27 permitted production units
justifications: The final narrowing order requires all of P1 and only the non-privileged subsection P3A. P3B is privileged and outside the production duty, while P2 and P4 were withdrawn.

concepts.name: WORK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request was delivered on 22 November, earlier than the termination trigger, so the ten-Business-Day period began on the next eligible day and expired on 8 December 2027. WORK-1 is an ordinary active copy, and the courtesy preservation request does not create a binding hold or restart the deadline.

concepts.name: BK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request delivered on 22 November is the earlier Section 7.1 trigger. BK-1 must be deleted by the earlier of its scheduled overwrite and 45 calendar days after that trigger; the scheduled overwrite on 30 December comes first, and restoration does not restart either deadline.

concepts.name: Artifacts permitted retention at the December snapshot
justifications: The segregated counsel-held archive qualifies for the archival exception, the immutable backup remains before its scheduled overwrite, and the exact bundle remains subject to a binding preservation order. WORK-1 is an ordinary active copy and NOTE-1 is not covered by a retention exception.

concepts.name: NOTE-1 model training permitted as residual knowledge
justifications: NOTE-1 contains deliberately recorded parameter values and reconstruction notes, which are excluded from residual-knowledge permission. Training with Confidential Information is prohibited without a separate signed licence, and none covers this use.
